facts.audience: busy parents who book check-ups for their kids
facts.problem: appointments get missed and the chair sits empty
facts.cause: the only reminder is an email sent the evening before, which many parents don't see until it is too late to rearrange (from the practice's own front-desk notes)
facts.solution: a text reminder two days ahead that patients can reply to, to confirm or reschedule
facts.outcome: when someone can't make it, they can tell the practice early, so the slot can be offered to another patient

headline: Booked check-ups,
empty chairs
chapters.narration: Check-ups get missed. Chairs sit empty.

headline: One evening email,
seen late
chapters.narration: Our only reminder: an evening email, seen late.

headline: Text early,
reply to reschedule
chapters.narration: We now text two days ahead. Reply to reschedule, so we can offer the slot.

events.text: Harbor Lane: check-up in two days
Text two days ahead to confirm

checks: Every fact comes from the brief. I added no prices, rates, statistics, guarantees or quotes.
No digits appear in on-screen text or narration. days_before 1 and 2 are compiler settings for 'evening before' and 'two days ahead', and they are never shown as text.
No forbidden words (guarantee, always, never, best, lowest, save) and no em or en dashes.
All six essential facts are present, so there are no questions.

Duration fix: the narration is now 29 words (6 + 8 + 15), down from 37. The pulse event is gone. Only one event (the chair becoming occupied) falls on the last word, 'slot', and nothing comes after it.
'Confirm' is kept in the checklist text and 'reschedule' in the narration and reply message, so the whole solution is still shown.
There are 4 objects. The chair (2x2), calendar (2x1) and phone (1x2) are large. The parent is 1x1. No overlaps: chair r1-2 c1-2, phone r1-2 c3, calendar r3 c1-2, parent r3c3.
The only callout is on the chair, which sits in row 1.
The phone-to-parent link is short (c3, vertically adjacent). The calendar remind arrow shows the reminder moving from the evening before to two days ahead.
Every object is drawn before it is changed or connected. c1 is created before it is broken or fixed.

Every 'on' word appears exactly in its chapter's narration: missed, Chairs, empty, reminder, email, seen, late, text, ahead, Reply, offer, slot. Each emphasis_on word (empty, late, Reply) is in its narration.
Text lengths are within limits: kickers up to 18 characters, headline lines up to 19, callout 19, link labels up to 19, messages up to 33, checklist 30.
Outcome: the narration keeps the brief's hedge ('so we can offer the slot'). The calendar's rebooked check and the filled chair show the freed slot going to another patient.
